walkthroughs.body_html:
Genetic Information & Variation — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Genetic Information & Variation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Genetic Information & Variation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The genetic code is described as 'degenerate' because:
options: It changes over time
Multiple codons code for the same amino acid
Codons overlap
Only one amino acid is coded
DNA template
Anticodon
Ribosomal RNA
Promoter

mcqs.q: What are the three repeated stages of one PCR cycle?
options: Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.
PCR has just one stage — heating the DNA until it copies itself.
Denaturation (high temp, strands separate), annealing (lower temp, primers bind), extension (Taq polymerase synthesises new strands).
PCR uses enzymes from bacteria to cut DNA into fragments, then sticks them back together.

mcqs.q: What is the role of the guide RNA in CRISPR-Cas9?
options: It directs Cas9 to the specific DNA sequence to cut by base-pairing with the target.
PCR uses enzymes from bacteria to cut DNA into fragments, then sticks them back together.
Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.
Guide RNA is the new sequence that gets inserted into the genome.

mcqs.q: What is the role of DNA ligase when inserting a gene into a plasmid?
options: DNA ligase reads the gene and translates it into protein.
Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.
It forms phosphodiester bonds that join the gene to the cut plasmid, sealing the recombinant DNA.
DNA ligase cuts the plasmid open so the gene can be inserted.
